similar_scenes.name: Original Dixieland Jazz Band y el jazz blanco
similar_scenes.author: Ted Gioia
similar_scenes.desc: Un grupo blanco de Nueva Orleans, la Original Dixieland Jazz Band de Nick LaRocca, hace en 1917 los primeros discos comerciales de jazz: Columbia duda, pero Victor publica «Livery Stable Blues» con gran éxito. Gioia rechaza tanto el revisionismo de LaRocca, que se presentaba como creador del jazz, como el desprecio de sus críticos: la corneta de LaRocca es sutil y el clarinete de Larry Shields marcó a Benny Goodman. Viajan a Inglaterra y Francia y popularizan la música. En Chicago, los New Orleans Rhythm Kings de Paul Mares imitan a los negros de su ciudad, con el clarinete lineal y melódico de Leon Roppolo, y en 1923 graban con Jelly Roll Morton la primera sesión interracial de Chicago.
similar_scenes.family: Nueva Orleans, Chicago y jazz clásico

podcast.title: New Orleans Popularity in 1917
podcast.body: New recordings of Dixieland Jazz proved to be very popular in and around New Orleans, spearheaded by groups like the Original Dixieland Jazz Band around 1917. "Their new recordings of this thing called Jazz proved to be pretty popular in and around New Orleans."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: History of the Modern Drum Kit

podcast.title: Emergence during World War I
podcast.body: Dixieland Jazz emerged around the same historical period as World War I. Its timeline places it as an early form of jazz, later to be revived as Trag Jazz. "This was a revival of something close to Dixieland Jazz from New Orleans, which emerged around the same time as World War I."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Origin in New Orleans
podcast.body: Dixieland Jazz originated in New Orleans, establishing its roots in American musical tradition. This genre served as a foundational influence for the later Trag Jazz movement. "This was a revival of something close to Dixieland Jazz from New Orleans, which emerged around the same time as World War I."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
